title: Νευρωνικά δίκτυα ενισχυμένα με KANB για πρόβλεψη κινητικότητας
abstract: Στη συγκεκριμένη εργασία εξετάζεται το αν εκπαιδεύσιμες συναρτήσεις ενεργοποίησης της οικογένειας KANB μπορούν να βελτιώσουν την πρόβλεψη θαλάσσιας κινητικότητας. Το πρόβλημα είναι η πρόβλεψη του αριθμού πλοίων σε συγκεκριμένα γεωγραφικά κελιά για έξι χρονικούς ορίζοντες των 5 λεπτών, μέχρι τα 30 λεπτά. Οι δέκα χρονοσειρές που χρησιμοποιούνται είναι από την περιοχή του Αιγαίου και της Βρέστης, ενώ κάθε κελί αντιμετωπίζεται και χρησιμοποιείται για εκπαίδευση ως ξεχωριστό πρόβλημα. Στα δεδομένα περιλαμβάνονται ο τρέχοντας αριθμός πλοίων, οι χρονικές υστερήσεις, οι μεταβλητές γειτονικών κελιών και ημερολογιακά χαρακτηριστικά. Εφόσον τα διαθέσιμα γνωρίσματα κάθε γειτονιάς δεν είναι κοινά και δεν έχουν το ίδιο σχήμα σε όλες τις περιοχές, η προεπεξεργασία των δεδομένων έγινε ανά κελί. Στο Αιγαίο υπήρχαν πολύ λίγα κενά, ενώ χρονικοί κάδοι που δεν υπήρχαν, αντιστοιχούσαν πρακτικά σε μηδενική κίνηση. Από την άλλη, στα δεδομένα της Βρέστης, οι μηδενικές τιμές υπήρχαν και αντιστοιχούσαν σε άγνωστες παρατηρήσεις. Έτσι έγινε μόνο περιορισμένη συμπλήρωση του μελλοντικού χρονικού ορίζοντα για κενά έως 15 λεπτά, με τα μεγαλύτερα διαστήματα να αφαιρούνται από την εκπαίδευση και την αξιολόγηση. Ο διαχωρισμός των δεδομένων έγινε με αναλογία 70/15/15 και ήταν χρονολογικός ώστε να μην εισάγεται πληροφορία από το μέλλον. Το μοντέλο είναι ένας Transformer δύο επιπέδων. Κάθε αριθμητικό γνώρισμα μετατρέπεται σε διάνυσμα 64 διαστάσεων και αντιμετωπίζεται ως ξεχωριστό token. Επομένως, ο μηχανισμός προσοχής μαθαίνει σχέσεις ανάμεσα στα γνωρίσματα και όχι ανάμεσα σε διαδοχικά χρονικά βήματα. Η χρονική πληροφορία βρίσκεται στις μεταβλητές υστέρησης. Η συνάρτηση ενεργοποίησης που εξετάζεται τοποθετείται στο feed-forward τμήμα κάθε Transformer block, με ανεξάρτητες παραμέτρους ανά επίπεδο. Συγκρίνονται οι KANB17, KANB18 και KANB21 με τις ReLU, GELU και ParametricGELU. Όλες οι υπόλοιπες επιλογές του μοντέλου παραμένουν σταθερές. Η πλήρης διαδικασία χωρίστηκε σε δύο στάδια. Αρχικά έγινε διαδοχική ρύθμιση υπερπαραμέτρων μόνο στο σύνολο επικύρωσης, με την KANB21 και πέντε χρονοσειρές ανάπτυξης. Κάθε φορά άλλαζε μία παράμετρος, ενώ το test set παρέμενε κλειστό. Επιλέχθηκαν learning rate 3 × 10− 4, Adam epsilon 10− 5, batch size 256, 150 epochs, depth 2 και 4 attention heads. Το early stopping δεν χρησιμοποιήθηκε και οι αρχικές τιμές των παραμέτρων KANB έμειναν αμετάβλητες. Η τελική αξιολόγηση περιλαμβάνει 300 εκπαιδεύσεις: δέκα χρονοσειρές, έξι συναρτήσεις ενεργοποίησης και πέντε τυχαίους σπόρους. Η GELU έχει το χαμηλότερο μέσο validation relative MAE (0,8037). Στο test set, η KANB17 έχει το χαμηλότερο μέσο relative MAE (0,8498), ενώ η ReLU κατατάσσεται πρώτη σε πέντε από τις δέκα χρονοσειρές. Οι διαφορές είναι μικρές: για παράδειγμα, η διαφορά KANB21–GELU είναι −0,0012 και δεν είναι στατιστικά τεκμηριωμένη (exact p = 0,912). Όλα τα διαστήματα εμπιστοσύνης των συγκρίσεων KANB με τις βασικές ενεργοποιήσεις περιλαμβάνουν το μηδέν. Το μοντέλο ξεπερνά την απλή πρόβλεψη επιμονής σε οκτώ χρονοσειρές, αλλά όχι στα Brest 74768 και 75108. Οι μαθημένες καμπύλες επιβεβαιώνουν ότι οι παράμετροι KANB ενημερώθηκαν σε κάθε Transformer block. Παρ’ όλα αυτά, η προσαρμογή τους δεν έδωσε σταθερό πλεονέκτημα στο MAE. Το ασφαλές συμπέρασμα είναι ότι οι KANB είναι ανταγωνιστικές εναλλακτικές με μικρή επιβάρυνση σε παραμέτρους, όχι καθολικά καλύτερες συναρτήσεις ενεργοποίησης για το συγκεκριμένο πρόβλημα. Σε έναν πρόσθετο έλεγχο με την KANB17 δοκιμάστηκαν batch size 512, ReduceLROnPlateau και μία επαναφορά του learning rate. Καμία από αυτές τις αλλαγές δεν βελτίωσε τη μέση επίδοση στο validation set σε σχέση με το αρχικό πρωτόκολλο, δηλαδή batch size 256 και σταθερό learning rate. Στην αξιολόγηση χρησιμοποιήθηκε επίσης το PEMS04, ένα σύνολο δεδομένων οδικής κυκλοφορίας με 307 αισθητήρες και παρατηρήσεις ανά 5 λεπτά. Κάθε χρονικό σημείο έχει 3 μεταβλητές: την κυκλοφοριακή ροή, πληρότητα και μέση ταχύτηταη . Στόχος αυτού του πειράματος ήταν να αξιολογηθούν οι KANB σε ένα διαφορετικό πρόβλημα κινητικότητας, με μη γραμμική συμπεριφορά καθώς και χωρική διασύνδεση μεταξύ των αισθητήρων. Καθώς η σύγκριση όλων των συνδυασμών μεταξύ των 307 αισθητήρων, με έξι ενεργοποιήσεις και 5 seeds θα χρειαζόταν 9210 runs, επιλέχθηκε ένα μικρό υποσύνολο. Η αρχική ομάδα υποψηφίων σχηματίστηκε μόνο από το training set, βάσει του απόλυτου και σχετικού σφάλματος της πρόβλεψης persistence. Στο validation set κρατήθηκαν οι αισθητήρες στους οποίους το μη γραμμικό Histogram Gradient Boosting ξεπερνούσε το Ridge και το persistence στον ορίζοντα των 30 λεπτών. Με αυτή τη διαδικασία επιλέχθηκαν και πάγωσαν οι αισθητήρες 202, 289, 303, 2 και 106. Το test set δεν χρησιμοποιήθηκε κατά την επιλογή. Κάθε δείγμα του PEMS04 περιλαμβάνει 71 γνωρίσματα: 36 πρόσφατες τιμές του αισθητήρα- στόχου, 24 πρόσφατες τιμές ροής από δύο γειτονικούς αισθητήρες, έξι ημερήσιες και εβδομαδιαίες υστερήσεις και πέντε ημερολογιακές μεταβλητές. Ο στόχος είναι η κυκλοφοριακή ροή στους ίδιους έξι χρονικούς ορίζοντες που χρησιμοποιήθηκαν στα ναυτιλιακά δεδομένα, από 5 έως 30 λεπτά. Το τελικό πείραμα περιλάμβανε 150 runs, δηλαδή πέντε αισθητήρες, έξι συναρτήσεις ενεργοποίησης και πέντε τυχαίους σπόρους. Η KANB18 πέτυχε το χαμηλότερο μέσο test relative MAE, με τιμή 0,747688, έναντι 0,749232 της ReLU και 0,750365 της GELU. Η KANB18 ήταν καλύτερη από τη GELU και στους μέσους όρους των πέντε αισθητήρων, σε 16 από τα 25 paired runs και σε πέντε από τους έξι χρονικούς ορίζοντες. Η συνολική βελτίωση έναντι της GELU ήταν 0,357%. Η διαφορά δεν έφτασε το συμβατικό επίπεδο στατιστικής σημαντικότητας, αφού ο ακριβής αμφίπλευρος έλεγχος έδωσε p=0,0625. Με μόνο πέντε ανεξάρτητους αισθητήρες, όμως, το πείραμα είχε περιορισμένη στατιστική ισχύ. Η κοινή κατεύθυνση του αποτελέσματος στους αισθητήρες και στους περισσότερους χρονικούς ορίζοντες αποτελεί θετική ένδειξη για την KANB18. Χρειάζεται αξιολόγηση σε μεγαλύτερο δείγμα αισθητήρων για να διαπιστωθεί αν το πλεονέκτημα διατηρείται και αποκτά ισχυρότερη στατιστική τεκμηρίωση.

title: Distance and similarity measures in multidimensional spaces and their use in multidimensional data clustering problems
abstract: Η ανάλυση κατά συστάδες αποτελεί έναν από τους σημαντικότερους κλάδους της Στατιστικής και της Επιστήμης των Δεδομένων, με εφαρμογές σε πλήθος επιστημονικών και τεχνολογικών πεδίων. Στόχος της είναι η ανακάλυψη υποκείμενης δομής και προτύπων, μέσα σε σύνολα δεδομένων, μέσω της ομαδοποίησης παρατηρήσεων που παρουσιάζουν ομοιότητες και της διάκρισης εκείνων που εμφανίζουν διαφοροποιήσεις. Καθοριστικό ρόλο σε αυτή τη διαδικασία διαδραματίζει η έννοια της απόστασης ή της ομοιότητας, καθώς το μέτρο που επιλέγεται για τον υπολογισμό της εγγύτητας μεταξύ αντικειμένων καθορίζει άμεσα το αποτέλεσμα και την ποιότητα της ομαδοποίησης. Η επιλογή διαφορετικών μετρικών αποστάσεων δύναται να οδηγήσει σε ουσιωδώς διαφορετικά αποτελέσματα, ακόμη και όταν εφαρμόζεται ο ίδιος αλγόριθμος clustering στο ίδιο σύνολο δεδομένων. Η διεθνής βιβλιογραφία περιγράφει μια πληθώρα εναλλακτικών μετρικών, από τις κλασικές Ευκλείδειες αποστάσεις έως πιο εξειδικευμένα μέτρα, όπως η απόσταση Mahalanobis ή οι δείκτες ομοιότητας τύπου Jaccard και Cosine. Κάθε μέτρο παρουσιάζει θεωρητικά πλεονεκτήματα και μειονεκτήματα, καθώς και διαφορετικό πεδίο εφαρμογής, γεγονός που καθιστά τη μελέτη και σύγκρισή τους αναγκαία για την κατανόηση της συμπεριφοράς τους σε πολυδιάστατους χώρους δεδομένων. Μέσα στο πλαίσιο αυτό, η παρούσα διπλωματική εργασία εστιάζει σε τρεις άξονες. Στη συστηματική παρουσίαση των σημαντικότερων μετρικών αποστάσεων και στα Μέτρα ομοιότητας που χρησιμοποιούνται στη βιβλιογραφία, με αναφορά στις μαθηματικές τους ιδιότητες και στις θεωρητικές σχέσεις που τις συνδέουν. Στην ανάλυση της σχέσης μεταξύ απόστασης και ομοιότητας, καθώς και της τεχνικής μετάβασης από το ένα μέτρο στο άλλο, με ιδιαίτερη έμφαση στις εφαρμογές που συναντώνται σε τεχνικές μηχανικής μάθησης και εξόρυξης δεδομένων. Στην πειραματική αξιολόγηση διαφορετικών μετρικών μέσω της εφαρμογής αλγορίθμων clustering σε πολυδιάστατα σύνολα δεδομένων, ώστε να αποτιμηθεί η αποτελεσματικότητά τους σε πραγματικά σενάρια. Η συνδυαστική θεώρηση θεωρίας και πράξης αναμένεται να προσφέρει μια ολοκληρωμένη εικόνα για τον ρόλο που διαδραματίζει η επιλογή μετρικής απόστασης στη διαδικασία της ομαδοποίησης. Με τον τρόπο αυτό, η εργασία στοχεύει όχι μόνο να φωτίσει τις θεωρητικές πτυχές του προβλήματος, αλλά και να προτείνει πρακτικές κατευθύνσεις για την ορθολογική επιλογή μετρικών ανάλογα με τα χαρακτηριστικά των δεδομένων και τις απαιτήσεις της εκάστοτε εφαρμογής.

Στόχος της είναι η ανακάλυψη υποκείμενης δομής και προτύπων, μέσα σε σύνολα δεδομένων, μέσω της ομαδοποίησης παρατηρήσεων που παρουσιάζουν ομοιότητες και της διάκρισης εκείνων που εμφανίζουν διαφοροποιήσεις. Καθοριστικό ρόλο σε αυτή τη διαδικασία διαδραματίζει η έννοια της απόστασης ή της ομοιότητας, καθώς το μέτρο που επιλέγεται για τον υπολογισμό της εγγύτητας μεταξύ αντικειμένων καθορίζει άμεσα το αποτέλεσμα και την ποιότητα της ομαδοποίησης. Η επιλογή διαφορετικών μετρικών αποστάσεων δύναται να οδηγήσει σε ουσιωδώς διαφορετικά αποτελέσματα, ακόμη και όταν εφαρμόζεται ο ίδιος αλγόριθμος clustering στο ίδιο σύνολο δεδομένων. Η διεθνής βιβλιογραφία περιγράφει μια πληθώρα εναλλακτικών μετρικών, από τις κλασικές Ευκλείδειες αποστάσεις έως πιο εξειδικευμένα μέτρα, όπως η απόσταση Mahalanobis ή οι δείκτες ομοιότητας τύπου Jaccard και Cosine. Κάθε μέτρο παρουσιάζει θεωρητικά πλεονεκτήματα και μειονεκτήματα, καθώς και διαφορετικό πεδίο εφαρμογής, γεγονός που καθιστά τη μελέτη και σύγκρισή τους αναγκαία για την κατανόηση της συμπεριφοράς τους σε πολυδιάστατους χώρους δεδομένων. Μέσα στο πλαίσιο αυτό, η παρούσα διπλωματική εργασία εστιάζει σε τρεις άξονες. Στην ανάλυση της σχέσης μεταξύ απόστασης και ομοιότητας, καθώς και της τεχνικής μετάβασης από το ένα μέτρο στο άλλο, με ιδιαίτερη έμφαση στις εφαρμογές που συναντώνται σε τεχνικές μηχανικής μάθησης και εξόρυξης δεδομένων. Στην πειραματική αξιολόγηση διαφορετικών μετρικών μέσω της εφαρμογής αλγορίθμων clustering σε πολυδιάστατα σύνολα δεδομένων, ώστε να αποτιμηθεί η αποτελεσματικότητά τους σε πραγματικά σενάρια. title: Federated Learning-Driven Collaborative Art-Data Analysis and Privacy Protection
abstract: Digital art platforms, AIGC systems, and cross-institutional design collaboration platforms continuously generate multimodal artistic creation data that are privacy-sensitive and distributed across many clients. Centralized modeling risks exposure while ordinary federated learning struggles with non-IID styles and gradient leakage. This study proposes SAP-FL, combining local multimodal training with gradient clipping, DP noise, secure aggregation, credibility-weighted aggregation, and compression for cross-node modeling without raw data leaving devices. On non-IID data, SAP-FL achieves F1 of 84.01% (vs. 81.74%/79.11% for FedAvg/DP-FedAvg), reduces membership inference success to 49.70% ( 20.10 points below FedAvg), and retains F1 of 82.36% at 200 clients. Grad-CAM shows SAP-FL consistently attends to brushstroke-dense regions and subject outlines.

title: Provenance-Native Audit Infrastructure for LLM-Maintained Wiki Knowledge Systems
abstract: LLM-maintained wiki systems accumulate structured knowledge by having a language model incrementally build and revise a persistent wiki layer over raw evidence sources. When such systems support decision-making in regulated domains, each output must be traceable to grounded evidence through an auditable chain. This paper presents a provenance-native architecture in which a dedicated provenance layer is embedded in the wiki’s operational loop, recording evidence bindings, claim versions, rule compilations, and decision traces as side effects of normal system operations. The architecture is organized around four technical components: (1) a typed provenance graph that binds claims to evidence passages with confidence-weighted edges; (2) a dual-layer diff mechanism combining textual and semantic comparison to detect silent LLM edits; (3) three confidence propagation strategies over multi-hop evidence–claim–rule–decision chains, compared on their suitability for regulatory communication; and (4) a retraction propagation engine that identifies all downstream dependents when upstream evidence is invalidated. We evaluate the system on a 112-document corpus producing 3174 graph nodes and 4398 edges. In controlled retraction experiments, the engine achieves 100% downstream recall with zero false propagation in under 600 ms per event. A sensitivity analysis over the human-review threshold parameter γ reveals a sharp phase transition in the fraction of flagged decisions, providing a concrete basis for negotiating review policies with regulators. An automated gap analysis shows the architecture demonstrates alignment with five of eight requirements derived from the EU AI Act and FDA AI/ML guidance, and we report module-level evaluations of claim extraction, evidence binding, and silent-edit detection together with a measured baseline comparison on retraction propagation. Code and experimental protocols will be released publicly upon publication.

title: True Alignment is Impossible: Holding the Goal Versus Satisfying the User
abstract: This paper makes one claim. True Alignment between a transformer's output and a requester's full goal is not reachable with the current architecture. The claim is structural. It does not depend on the quality of any model. It does not depend on the skill of any developer. The paper defines True Alignment as the output holding the requester's complete set of interacting constraints. It defines a second and weaker condition, casual alignment, as the requester accepting the output. The paper states that casual alignment is reachable and that True Alignment is not. The reason is that the requester's complete constraint set is never a full input to the process, and that the process erodes even the partial goal that was supplied. The paper does not present this as a defect to be blamed. It presents it as a property of the architecture that determines how the architecture must be used. The correct use is transformation of supplied material, not the pursuit of a goal the process cannot hold. The paper ends with the working method that follows from the claim.

title: Teaching the Colossus to Say No: A Critical Survey Review of Alignment Strategies for Large Language Models
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Alignment Strategies for Large Language Models in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of alignment and large language models as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Project Proposal for LMU Munich: DeepTech Software Architecture for Investment Recovery Probability (IRP) Diagnostics in Synergy with Tier-1 Partner Networks
abstract: The subject of the official municipal response regarding this project is formally defined as the "Strategic Initiative to Strengthen Munich's Economic Capacity". This strategic R&D Project Proposal and Executive Summary outlines the theoretical, financial, and architectural foundations for the deployment of a breakthrough DeepTech software solution utilizing advanced AI orchestration layers. Engineered as a specialized B2B White Label diagnostic service tailored for Tier-1 / Big-4 consulting networks and institutional insurers, the technology targets the global phenomenon of capital destruction in investment planning, which currently threatens over $1.12 trillion of Direct Investments annually. Operationally solving Daniel Kahneman’s Prospect Theory (Nobel Prize in Economics, 2002) at the enterprise and business-planning level, the framework will digitize investor risk thresholds via precise Investment Recovery Probability (IRP) diagnostics. This document serves as an official technical submission (an Executive Summary of the business plan) currently under institutional review at the Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München (LMU Munich). Crucially, this proposal was generated as a direct consequence of the recommendations outlined in the official response from the City of Munich’s Department of Labor and Economic Affairs (Landeshauptstadt München, Referat für Arbeit und Wirtschaft, signed by Dr. C. Scharpf, official communication dated May 20, 2026).

title: Dynamic Semantic Graph Evolution Algorithm (DSGEA)
abstract: Knowledge graphs (KGs) are increasingly utilized for representing and reasoning about complex information. However, traditional knowledge graph construction and maintenance methods often struggle to adapt to evolving semantic relationships, leading to outdated and inaccurate representations. This paper introduces the Dynamic Semantic Graph Evolution Algorithm (DSGEA), a novel approach leveraging reinforcement learning to achieve adaptive optimization of knowledge graphs. DSGEA employs graph neural networks (GNNs) to learn latent representations of nodes and edges within the KG. These representations are then utilized by a reinforcement learning agent to dynamically adjust the graph's connections and structure based on access patterns and semantic consistency feedback. This mimics the natural evolution of knowledge graphs, addressing the long-standing challenge of KG staleness. The core claim of this work is that a static KG structure is inherently inadequate for representing evolving semantics, and DSGEA provides a viable solution. The mechanism involves GNN-based representation learning coupled with a reinforcement learning agent for dynamic structural adaptation. The novelty lies in the integration of these techniques to establish an adaptive evolution mechanism for KGs, moving beyond static construction or rule-based updates. The algorithm's ability to learn and respond to changes in the KG ensures its ongoing relevance and accuracy.

title: Adaptive Algorithm Tree Semantic Representation Learning
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive algorithm tree semantic representation learning method based on deep learning. Traditional algorithm tree learning methods typically rely on predefined structures, while this approach leverages an adaptive deep learning model to learn data structure potentials, thereby enhancing semantic reasoning. We propose a novel approach that dynamically adjusts model parameters to capture complex semantic nuances within the data. The core mechanism involves learning a latent semantic representation of the data using a deep neural network, followed by an adaptive optimization process that fine-tunes the model to improve accuracy in semantic inference. This work demonstrates improved performance on several benchmark datasets, highlighting the benefits of this adaptive approach.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Topology Transformation Algorithm
abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating field of physics, offers a unique framework for understanding and manipulating quantum systems. Traditional quantum transformations, however, often struggle to effectively model and analyze complex topological structures. This paper introduces an innovative algorithm, the Adaptive Quantum Topology Transformation Algorithm (AQTTA), designed to address this challenge. AQTTA leverages the inherent dynamic nature of quantum topology, employing self-adaptive transformation parameters to optimize the calculation process and significantly enhance computational efficiency. This novel approach distinguishes itself from existing quantum transformation methods through its ability to dynamically adjust transformation parameters based on the evolving topology, enabling more robust and efficient modeling of complex quantum systems. The core mechanism centers around the exploitation of quantum topology's inherent responsiveness, leading to a fundamentally different algorithmic strategy. The paper details the algorithm's design, performance analysis, and potential applications across various quantum computational tasks.

title: Multi-Body Quantum Field Theory Adaptive Geometry Expansion
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of adaptive geometry expansion in multi-body quantum field theory (MQFT) to enhance the precision of modeling quantum system behavior and uncover correlations between the geometric structure of quantum systems and quantum computation performance. Traditional MQFT approaches predominantly focus on multi-state dynamics, and this work introduces this technique to improve the predictive accuracy of quantum system behavior. The core mechanism involves extending the system's geometric structure through adaptive calculations, revealing the relationship between these geometric features and quantum computation performance. This research offers a novel approach to tackling challenges in quantum system design and optimization.

title: 拓扑群的自适应量子纠缠计算
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum entanglement computation based on topological group dynamics. Traditional methods often rely on static computation, while this work proposes a method that dynamically adjusts the topological group to influence the entanglement state. We aim to significantly enhance the accuracy and efficiency of quantum entanglement calculations by leveraging this dynamic adjustment. The core mechanism involves meticulously manipulating the topology of a topological group to achieve precise entanglement manipulations. This results in a more robust and adaptable system for quantum information processing.

title: Brandt's Hedgehog: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Hedgehog's Behavior
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Brandt's Hedgehog, inspired by the foraging behavior of hedgehogs. Hedgehogs exhibit a distinctive strategy of repeatedly searching a limited area before moving to a new one, effectively balancing exploration and exploitation. The algorithm leverages this behavior to construct a search space and iteratively refine solutions. Brandt's Hedgehog utilizes a 'territory' concept, where a solution is associated with a defined area. The algorithm dynamically adjusts the size of these territories and the frequency of territory transitions based on the population's convergence and the quality of the best solution. The core mechanism involves a probabilistic selection of territories, followed by a local search process within that territory. We present the algorithm's design, detailing the key parameters and their impact on performance. Experimental results on several benchmark optimization problems demonstrate that Brandt's Hedgehog exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems with local optima and where a nuanced balance between exploration and exploitation is crucial. The algorithm's simplicity and intuitive inspiration from a natural phenomenon make it a promising addition to the metaheuristic toolbox.

title: Bramble Cay Melomys-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Bramble Cay Melomys-Inspired Metaheuristic (BCMM), designed to tackle complex optimization challenges. The algorithm draws inspiration from the remarkable survival strategies of *Melomys rubicola* on Bramble Cay, a low-lying island in the Torres Strait. Specifically, the algorithm mimics the animal's adaptive relocation behavior in response to rising sea levels, incorporating dynamic adjustment of solution parameters and a novel exploration-exploitation balance mechanism. The BCMM algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a swarm of agents that iteratively refine solutions. The core components include a dynamic parameter adjustment scheme, influenced by the perceived 'threat' level (analogous to sea level rise) and a 'relocation' operator, which strategically adjusts individual agent parameters based on solution quality and diversity. Mathematical formulations for key aspects of the algorithm, including the dynamic parameter update rule and the relocation operator, are presented. The performance of the BCMM algorithm is evaluated on a set of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive advantages compared to established metaheuristic methods such as Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization. The results indicate that BCMM exhibits robust performance across a range of problem types, showcasing its potential for practical applications in diverse fields.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Quantum-Enhanced Graph Neural Networks (QEN) presents a novel approach to graph neural network (GNN) learning, leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement to enhance both the training process and the network's expressive capabilities. This research investigates a method for utilizing entanglement to accelerate training and improve the network's ability to represent complex relationships within graph data. We introduce a new architecture incorporating quantum entanglement-enhanced layer activations, exploring its potential to overcome limitations inherent in classical GNN training. The core mechanism focuses on utilizing entanglement to reduce computational complexity and improve the speed of learning. This work demonstrates promising results through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation, suggesting a significant improvement in both training speed and model performance.

title: Inverse Kolmogorov Complexity for Data Compression
abstract: This paper explores the application of Inverse Kolmogorov Complexity (IKC) to data compression, aiming to identify the most efficient representation of a given dataset. We propose a novel algorithm based on gradient-based inverse Kolmogorov complexity, designed to minimize the number of bits required to represent the data. The core mechanism centers around iteratively refining a representation by minimizing the information lost during compression, with a focus on identifying and exploiting inherent data redundancy. We analyze the algorithm's potential for superior compression ratios compared to existing techniques, considering various data characteristics and highlighting the benefits of this approach. This research investigates the effectiveness of this method through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental testing.

title: Title: Dynamic Topology in Variational Quantum Algorithms for Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the implementation of a dynamic topology controller within variational quantum algorithms designed for optimization. Current variational quantum algorithms often suffer from limitations imposed by the underlying hardware, hindering efficient exploration of solution spaces. We propose a novel approach leveraging a 'topology controller' that dynamically adjusts the algorithm's search parameters – specifically circuit depth – in real-time based on the hardware's capabilities. The core claim is that this dynamic adaptation will significantly improve the efficiency of optimization, particularly in scenarios where hardware constraints are a major factor. The paper details the design of the topology controller, explores its impact on algorithm performance, and presents preliminary results demonstrating the potential for enhanced exploration.

title: Formal Verification of a Memory Allocator for Rust Hypervisors: From Verified to Deployable Code with Functional Equivalence Guarantees
abstract: Bugs in hypervisor memory management may lead to double allocation, physical aliasing, or violations of inter-VM isolation. This paper studies BitAllocCascade16, a bitmap-based frame allocator used on real hypervisors implemented in Rust. We use Verus to formally verify the allocator, proving its structural invariants and functional correctness. In the process, we uncover and fix a shift-operation overflow bug in the original implementation. Source-level verification often requires proof-oriented refactoring, which may cause the verified implementation to diverge from the original deployable code in structure, interface, and performance characteristics. To address this integration gap, we formulate the relation between the verified and original programs as a functional equivalence problem, and introduce Veri-easy, a lightweight and automated framework for establishing such equivalence. Guided by performance analysis, we further derive a final implementation and qualify it against the verified version. Our results show that the verified allocator faithfully matches the behavior of the original, and that the final implementation can be integrated into hvisor and HyperEnclave without compromising correctness or performance.

title: Adaptive Record-Length Covert Channels in IoT Environments: Hiding Botnet Communication in TLS 1.3
abstract: TLS 1.3 verschlüsselt fast alle Handshake- und Anwendungsdaten nach dem ClientHello. Ein passiver Beobachter sieht dennoch die Record-Längen, die eine Vorgängerarbeit nutzte, um eine binäre Nutzlast in einem Mirai-Bot-/Command-and-Control-(C2)-Kanal zu kodieren. Diese Kodierungen — binaryCCfixed und binaryCCprevious — wurden nie an IoT-Verkehr angepasst, sodass offen bleibt, ob sie von harmlosem IoT-TLS ununterscheidbar gemacht werden können. Diese Arbeit untersucht, wie sich ein stabiler Fingerabdruck der WAN-IoT-TLS 1.3-Record-Längen pro Flow bilden lässt, inwieweit ein verteilungsbewusster Generator die Vorgänger-Kodierungen in Richtung dieses Fingerabdrucks lenken kann und wie sich sechs statistische Sampler hinsichtlich Wiedergabetreue, Neuanpassung und Kosten vergleichen. Die Methode ist empirisch. Eine Baseline von 4 361 WAN-IoT-Flows (95 464 Records) wird durch einen elfdimensionalen Fingerabdruck pro Flow charakterisiert, der nach dem gruppenübergreifenden Variationskoeffizienten geordnet ist. Die Kodierungen werden festgehalten. Ein fünfschichtiger Generator zieht Längen aus einer Zielform, erzwingt den bit-korrekten Bereich, steuert laufende Momente und segmentiert lange C2-Sitzungen in kurze virtuelle Flows. Sechs Sampler — Piecewise CDF, Maximum Entropy, KDE-Resampling, GMM-Sampling, GLD-Fitting und Rejection — implementieren die Formschicht hinter einer gemeinsamen Schnittstelle. Jeder Lauf wird anhand derselben Baseline mit dem 1-Wasserstein-Abstand, Momentfehlern und einem Hauptkomponenten-Ausreißertest bei einer Falsch-Positiv-Rate von 5% bewertet. Die engen Merkmale des Fingerabdrucks (q25, min, median) müssen auf wenige Bytes genau getroffen werden. Die Neugestaltung reduziert jeden führenden Fehler der Randverteilung gegenüber dem Vorgängeransatz um mehr als die Hälfte (mittlerer Fehler 2,6×/11,2× bei den beiden Trägern; W1 etwa 2,2× bei beiden), doch eine multivariate Ununterscheidbarkeit wird nicht erreicht: Auch im besten Lauf lassen sich 88% der Flows über Unterschiede in q25 erkennen. Maximum Entropy und GLD-Fitting dominieren die Wiedergabetreue; zusammen mit Piecewise CDF bilden sie die Pareto-optimale Menge.

title: IBotAcademy, a Learning Environment to Learn Skills and Competences in Mobile and Manipulator Robotics Using a Problem-Based Learning Methodology in the Industry 4.0 Education
abstract: Smart industries base their development, maintenance, and operation on technologies compatible with what is known as Industry 4.0. In this context, the education sector needs the implementation of new learning schemes and environments for conceptual and practical learning, thereby supporting students’ training to help in the industrial digital transformation. The main contributions of this work are a learning environment for robotics that integrates software applications that quantitatively measure the student’s learning process; a competence framework focused on learning robotics, ROS background, and developing pickup/delivery tasks very common in the Industry 4.0 context; and a learning path implemented in step-by-step guided documentation that considers the competence framework proposed and progressively teaches ROS concepts. This work also describes the development of the learning environment and the software tools that support the student’s learning process. Two pilot tests were performed on iBotAcademy considering twenty students of the Universidad del Valle. The iBotAcademy mobile robotics and the manipulator robotics learning paths achieved an average of 82% positive answers, and 99% positive answers, respectively. The average coefficients of variation of these tests were 16.4% and 8.3%, showing high data consistency. Then, the iBotAcademy learning environment helps to train students for the industrial digital transformation.

title: A Hierarchical Benchmarking Framework for Homomorphic Encryption-Based Aggregation and Validation Using Real Smart Meter Data
abstract: Homomorphic encryption (HE) enables computation on encrypted data and has emerged as a promising technology for privacy-preserving distributed analytics. However, the practical deployment of HE in large-scale hierarchical systems requires a thorough understanding of its computational overhead, scalability, and accuracy. This paper presents a generic hierarchical benchmarking framework for systematically evaluating homomorphic encryption schemes in multi-level aggregation environments. The framework supports configurable aggregation topologies, detailed operation-level profiling, and multiple encryption backends, enabling consistent and reproducible performance analysis across node-, cluster-, and global-level aggregation stages. Using the proposed framework, we conduct a comparative evaluation of the Brakerski/Fan–Vercauteren (BFV) and Cheon–Kim–Kim–Song (CKKS) schemes under identical workloads. Experimental results show that CKKS consistently outperforms BFV, achieving a 44.3% reduction in aggregation latency and a 24.6% reduction in decryption latency. For the tested encoding and parameter settings, CKKS delivers significantly lower numerical error, reducing the mean absolute error from 3.21×10−3 to 5.91×10−10. The proposed framework offers a reusable and extensible platform for evaluating emerging HE schemes and privacy-preserving analytics applications, thereby supporting future research and deployment of secure distributed data processing systems.

title: Engineering and Automatic Construction of the Knowledge Graph “Mathematical Equations”
abstract: Abstract We propose an approach to engineering and implementing a knowledge graph for representing and storing knowledge on mathematical equations. We have developed a knowledge graph prototype that represents knowledge about the main types of mathematical equations, including algebraic equations, ordinary differential equations, partial differential equations, and integral equations. We have designed a knowledge graph of mathematical equations as a mathematical artifact. We are integrating this artifact into the digital ecosystem of the Lobachevskii Digital Mathematical Library; therefore, we take into account the ecosystem’s general compatibility requirements during the design. We have developed software tools for extracting and processing information about equations presented in digital libraries and electronic scientific resources. The current version of the knowledge graph prototype is based on the OntoMathPRO ontology of professional mathematics and a taxonomy of equations, built on information extracted from the web pages of the portal EqWorld “The World of Mathematical Equations.” We expanded the OntoMathPRO ontology with new equation classes and new relationships to align with the equation type hierarchy presented on the EqWorld portal. We implemented a set of software modules that support the full cycle of knowledge graph generation, including a module for automatically extracting entities from external sources, a module for linking entities to OntoMathPRO ontology concepts, and a module for converting the acquired knowledge into an RDF representation and then storing it in a data warehouse. The knowledge graph supports SPARQL queries.

title: Kural Tabanlı Etiketleme ile Youtube Başlıklarında Clickbait Tespiti ve Sınıflandırma Analizi
abstract: Bu çalışmada, YouTube platformundaki video başlıklarından oluşan etiketsiz bir veri kümesinde clickbait (tıklanma tuzağı) içeriklerinin otomatik olarak sınıflandırılması amaçlanmıştır. Etiketleme süreci, literatürde tanımlanan clickbait göstergelerine dayalı olarak geliştirilen kural tabanlı bir puanlama sistemi ile gerçekleştirilmiştir. Her başlık için yapısal ve dilsel özellikler (rakam kullanımı, büyük harf oranı, noktalama yoğunluğu, duygusal kalıplar vb.) dikkate alınarak clickbait skoru hesaplanmış ve belirlenen eşik değeri üzerinden sınıflandırma yapılmıştır. Önerilen etiketleme yaklaşımının güvenilirliği, insan doğrulayıcılar ile gerçekleştirilen uyum analizi (Cohen’s Kappa) ile desteklenmiştir. Elde edilen etiketli veri üzerinde Lojistik Regresyon, Destek Vektör Makineleri, K-En Yakın Komşu, Rastgele Orman, Gradient Boosting ve XGBoost makine öğrenmesi algoritmaları uygulanmıştır. Modeller, doğruluk, kesinlik, duyarlılık, F1 skoru ve ROC-AUC metrikleriyle değerlendirilmiş; GridSearchCV yöntemiyle hiperparametre optimizasyonu gerçekleştirilmiştir. Sonuçlar, ensemble tabanlı algoritmaların (özellikle XGBoost ve Random Forest) en yüksek performansı gösterdiğini ortaya koymuştur. Betimleyici istatistikler ve t-testi bulguları, clickbait başlıkların daha kısa, daha fazla noktalama işareti içeren ve büyük harfli ifadelerle vurgulanan yapılara sahip olduğunu göstermiştir. Bu yönüyle çalışma, etiketsiz metin verilerinde insan etiketlemesi gerektirmeden uygulanabilir, açıklanabilir ve ölçeklenebilir bir yaklaşım sunmaktadır.

title: Knowledge Graph Completion Integrating Relational Context Semantics
authors: ZHAI Sheping, MA Mengyao, ZHANG Wenjing, YANG Rui
abstract: Existing Knowledge Graph Completion (KGC) methods fail to effectively distinguish semantic differences among paths at different levels and cannot dynamically adjust relation representations by fully leveraging neighborhood context information. Consequently, contextual semantics remain insufficiently understood. To address these issues, this paper proposes a KGC model integrating relational context semantics, named RCSKGC, for enhancing the semantic representation of learned paths and neighborhood information. First, the local and global encoding of multi-hop paths at different levels is performed using a Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (Bi-GRU) and an attention mechanism to extract effective path information. Meanwhile, the fine-grained semantic features of the path information at different levels are further enhanced through relational embedding contrastive learning. Second, a dual-attention mechanism and dynamic weighting strategy are employed to capture the neighborhood-level information of relations and learn their semantics through a "neighborhood—entity—relation" approach. Finally, the two types of relational representations are aggregated and used as inputs for the decoder to perform KGC. The results of experiments on the FB15k-237 dataset demonstrate that, compared to the best results of the baseline methods, RCSKGC achieves improvements of 1.4, 0.8, 1.3, and 2.1 percentage points in the Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), Hits@1, Hits@3, and Hits@10, respectively. Further, on the WN18RR dataset, RCSKGC shows improvements of 0.8 and 1.0 percentage points in MRR and Hits@3, respectively. These results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: LungGPT: A unified multimodal system for interpretable diagnosis and clinical decision support of respiratory diseases
abstract: Respiratory diseases cause significant morbidity, yet diagnosis remains labor intensive and dependent on physician expertise. Here, we present LungGPT, a unified multimodal system trained on 147 million tokens of domain-specific electronic health records from 125,917 participants. LungGPT comprises two modules: LungGPT-Dx for respiratory disease diagnosis and early warning of critical illness, and LungGPT-Ex for interpretable diagnostic reasoning and treatment recommendations. In large-scale evaluations, LungGPT-Dx achieves a macro-average area under the curve (AUC) of 0.852 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.839-0.865) across 22 respiratory diseases, with disease-specific AUCs exceeding 0.900 for lung cancer and pulmonary tuberculosis. Crucially, the model further improves early warning of critical illness by incorporating chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning into textual data and integrating computed tomography (CT) imaging features. LungGPT-Ex generates high-quality, interpretable reasoning that outperforms specialized clinical models and matches advanced general-purpose models such as GPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1 in correctness, completeness, and truthfulness. By bridging precision diagnostics and rapid decision-making, LungGPT provides a standardized framework to enhance clinical workflows and improve patient outcomes in respiratory healthcare.

title: A joint photovoltaic–load forecasting method with condition-guided spatio-temporal graph learning and controlled feature interaction
abstract: Distributed photovoltaic (PV) generation and active power demand jointly affect the net active power demand of distribution networks. However, PV and load forecasting rely on different predictive information, and direct cross-task information sharing may interfere with the learning of their respective representations. This study proposes a joint PV–load forecasting method that combines condition-guided spatio-temporal graph learning with controlled source–load feature interaction. Forecast meteorological information is used to guide historical PV feature aggregation, while periodic reference information guides historical load feature aggregation. The resulting representations interact through mapped and adaptively adjusted features, with stop-gradient controlling backpropagation through the interaction paths. PV, load, and net active power demand losses are further coordinated through uncertainty weighting. Experiments on two actual distribution networks show that the proposed method achieves lower PV and load forecasting errors than the corresponding single-task models and other multi-task baselines across the evaluated forecast horizons. evidence.title: A joint photovoltaic–load forecasting method with condition-guided spatio-temporal graph learning and controlled feature interaction
evidence.abstract: Distributed photovoltaic (PV) generation and active power demand jointly affect the net active power demand of distribution networks. However, PV and load forecasting rely on different predictive information, and direct cross-task information sharing may interfere with the learning of their respective representations. This study proposes a joint PV–load forecasting method that combines condition-guided spatio-temporal graph learning with controlled source–load feature interaction. Forecast meteorological information is used to guide historical PV feature aggregation, while periodic reference information guides historical load feature aggregation. The resulting representations interact through mapped and adaptively adjusted features, with stop-gradient controlling backpropagation through the interaction paths. PV, load, and net active power demand losses are further coordinated through uncertainty weighting. Experiments on two actual distribution networks show that the proposed method achieves lower PV and load forecasting errors than the corresponding single-task models and other multi-task baselines across the evaluated forecast horizons. Ablation experiments support the contributions of condition-guided feature extraction, controlled source–load interaction, and joint optimization. The proposed method also yields lower net active power demand errors when the PV and load forecasts are considered together. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for joint PV–load forecasting.

title: An Enhanced Convolution Transformer With Ladder Self‐Attention for Breast Cancer Histopathological Image Classification and Recurrence Prediction
abstract: ABSTRACT The most common cancer that kills women worldwide is breast cancer. Early detection of breast cancer and the prediction of recurrence is essential for diagnosis because metastasis and recurrence account for the majority of cancer‐related deaths. Images from the BreakHis dataset are gathered because physicians frequently use histopathological images to classify breast cancer. It takes a pathologist and specialists to grade histopathological images, and the process is inaccurate and time‐consuming. Therefore, using a score‐based VGG‐16 model, an improved convolution transformer with ladder self‐attention was developed for the purpose of classifying breast cancer histopathological images and predicting recurrence. Initially, the images are pre‐processed using a color deconvolution filter. Convolution transformers with Ladder Self‐Attention units and attention‐aware frequency domain transformers are used to extract spatial and frequency features from the pre‐processed images. The adaptive fusion module combines the multi‐scale features, which are then fed to the softmax classifier to classify images as benign or malignant. Using the greylag goose optimization (GGO) algorithm, the model's parameters are adjusted to produce better classification results. Next, by merging the cancerous images from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) dataset and the BreakHis dataset, recurrence is predicted. Recurrence is predicted using clinical and image features. Finally, it evaluated the performance of the proposed framework. The accuracy obtained by the proposed method is 99%, precision is 98.5%, recall is 98%, f ‐score is 98.2%, and MCC is 98%.

title: Emergence of Fibrations, Compression, and Symmetry Breaking in Artificial Neural Networks
abstract: Artificial neural networks are often regarded as powerful yet opaque black boxes. Here, we demonstrate that learning in deep neural networks generates local symmetries known in graph theory as fibrations and coverings. We prove that covering symmetries are stable attractors of stochastic gradient descent. Consistent with this theory, we report the emergence of covering symmetries across major network architectures, including multilayer, convolutional, recurrent, and transformer networks. Exploiting these symmetries enables drastic model compression - reducing networks to 17% of their original size without sacrificing performance. Furthermore, controlled breaking of covering symmetry overcomes the loss of plasticity, achieving state-of-the-art performance in continual learning. The theoretical results provide a new foundation for AI systems based on symmetries that convert black boxes into interpretable colored graphs and enable more efficient inference and lifelong learning.

title: TempCloze: Can Video-LLMs Identify the Missing Middle?
abstract: Temporal reasoning benchmarks for Video-LLMs are often mediated by language, leaving room for linguistic shortcuts from option wording, answer correlations, or language priors. To reduce such shortcuts, we introduce TempCloze, a video cloze benchmark for evaluating visual temporal reasoning in Video-LLMs. Given the beginning and ending clips of a video, models must identify the true missing middle from four candidates. TempCloze contains 1,521 carefully filtered videos from seven sources, mainly long-take and egocentric videos. We construct same-source distractors along three dimensions: Semantic asks what event should happen, Alignment probes when it should occur, and Progression tests how it should unfold, while shared scenes and objects reduce appearance cues. Our evaluation of 10 proprietary and 21 open-source Video-LLMs reveals Alignment as the primary bottleneck: models often recognize plausible semantic content and local event progression but struggle with temporal alignment. We further conduct error pattern and behavioral sensitivity analyses on TempCloze-Mixed and TempCloze-Hard with four representative models to examine where errors arise and how candidate order, context direction, visible span, frame density, and test-time scaling influence model choices.

title: Quantum LDPC and High-Rate CSS Codes from Fair-Density Parity-Check Codes
abstract: We construct quantum LDPC (qLDPC) and high-rate CSS codes from our recently introduced classical fair-density parity-check (FDPC) codes. To this end, we introduce a structured sparsification of FDPC parity-check matrices, which reduces their check weights while preserving the underlying combinatorial structure and distance guarantees. Combined with the hypergraph-product construction, this yields finite-length qLDPC codes with analytically controlled blocklength, dimension, certified distance, and stabilizer weight. For quantum blocklengths $N<10^5$, the constructions introduced here span guaranteed rates from approximately $0.35\%$ to $25.8\%$ and certified quantum distances from $12$ to $69$, with stabilizer weights between $8$ and $16$. In the large-blocklength regime, allowing the FDPC order and sparsified check weight to scale moderately with blocklength yields a family of high-rate CSS codes, which we refer to as quantum FDPC (qFDPC) codes, with rate $R_Q$ and minimum distance $D$ satisfying \[ R_Q = 1-O\left(\frac{1}{\log\log N}\right), \ \ D=Ω(N^{1/4}), \] and stabilizer weight $O(\log N\log\log N)$. Finally, the analytically available FDPC weight distribution provides explicit information about the logical operators of the resulting hypergraph-product codes. Over the quantum erasure channel, this structure yields rigorous first-order maximum likelihood (ML) expressions and a higher-order weight-distribution approximation to the ML logical block error probability. This enables estimation of finite-length operating points and the onset of the error-floor regime. To the best of our knowledge, beyond surface-code-type constructions, this is the first finite-rate qLDPC framework to provide both finite-length certified minimum-distance information and an analytical characterization of low-weight logical multiplicities.

title: Combined spatially and temporally multiplexed photonic reservoir computer with a diffractively coupled VCSEL-array
abstract: Abstract We report and analyse the classification performance of an experimental hybrid spatio-temporal photonic reservoir computer based upon a free-space vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser array. We demonstrate experimentally the enhancement of spatial-only reservoir operation, featuring the diffractive coupling of lasers in an external cavity, by exploiting up to 88 virtual nodes with time multiplexing. We analyse the dependence of performance on the spatial and virtual node number, and achieve an improvement for both spatial- and temporal-only reservoirs with a reduced test error of 0.026 in a classification task. Further, given the high bandwidth of the non-linear laser transformation, we demonstrate the expansion of an 11 spatial node network to a 968 node network, operating at an input time of 17.6 ns, maintaining high processing speed and improving network scalability and performance.

title: Implementation of uncertainty information to the CAMS radiation service irradiance estimates
abstract: A probabilistic error model was developed by the CAMS team (Lezaca et. al, 2025), which is able to provide uncertainty information on the CRS irradiance estimates. For this model, an extensive database of quality controlled irradiance ground observations was created and used to condition the cumulative distribution function of the CRS estimates deviations (CRS estimates - observations) of selected CRS model inputs. By applying this model on CRS user requests for solar irradiance time series, a complete error probability distribution can be delivered on every location and time step requested. This poster shows how to use this uncertainty informaiton on real case applications, that is, the generation of possible realistaions of the CRS estimates using probabilistic inference and the use of the uncertatiny information on the well established commercial PV modeling software PVSyst.

title: تأثير استراتيجيات التخصيص في التسويق المعتمد على الذكاء الاصطناعي في سلوك الشراء الاندفاعي: الدور الوسيط للاستثارة العاطفية و الثقة الرقمية
abstract: في عصر التسويق الالكتروني المعتمد على الذكاء الاصطناعي، تؤدي استراتيجيات التخصيص دوراً محورياً في التأثير على سلوك المستهلك. و وفقاً لمعيار (المحفز- الكائن- الاستجابة) و الذي يرمز له (S-O-R) فقد تم اختبار الابعاد ، إذ تسعى الدراسة لفحص كيفية تأثير الابعاد المتصلة بـ (الدقة ، التنوع ، الملاءمة (التجارب ذات الصلة) ، التوقيت) على سلوك الشراء الاندفاعي و دور المحفزات الرقمية في تحقيق عمليات الشراء العفوية عبر الإنترنت. وقد استعمل المنهج الكمي باستعمال استبيان منظم، وتم تحليل إجابات 475 مشتركا في برنامج SPSS 27 لإثبات صحة النموذج من خلال اختبار الموثوقية، واختبار KMO، وتحليل العوامل الاستكشافية. وطُبق تحليل الوساطة باستعمال PROCESS Macro النموذج 4 لاختبار تأثير استراتيجيات التخصيص على سلوك الشراء الاندفاعي. تكشف النتائج أن الدقة والملائمة (التجارب ذات الصلة) وتوقيت الزمن تؤثر بشكل كبير على سلوك الشراء الإلكتروني، بينما لا يظهر التنوع تأثيرا ملحوظا. كما وتسلط النتائج الضوء على التأثير غير المتساوي لاستراتيجيات التخصيص المختلفة وتوفر رؤى قيمة لتحسين أنظمة التوصيات المدعومة بالذكاء الاصطناعي وتحفيز سلوك الشراء الاندفاعي. كما تشجع الدراسة على إجراء أبحاث مستقبلية تدمج العوامل النفسية والسياقية مع سلوك الشراء.

title: Rancang Bangun AI Assistant Berbasis Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) untuk Layanan Informasi Akademik Fakultas
abstract: Perkembangan Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) memberikan peluang untuk meningkatkan akses terhadap informasi akademik melalui interaksi berbasis bahasa alami. Namun, penggunaan Large Language Model (LLM) secara langsung memiliki keterbatasan karena model dapat menghasilkan informasi yang tidak sesuai dengan sumber pengetahuan yang digunakan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk merancang dan membangun FEB AI Assistant sebagai layanan informasi akademik berbasis web pada Fakultas Ekonomi Universitas Negeri Jakarta (FEB UNJ) dengan menerapkan pendekatan Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Metode penelitian meliputi analisis kebutuhan, perancangan sistem, pembangunan knowledge base, implementasi RAG, pengembangan aplikasi, dan pengujian sistem. FEB AI Assistant dikembangkan menggunakan Laravel, PHP, MySQL, REST API, dan Gemini API sebagai LLM. Knowledge base dibangun dari dokumen akademik yang diproses menjadi document chunk untuk digunakan dalam proses retrieval sebelum menghasilkan respons. Hasil implementasi menunjukkan bahwa sistem dapat menjalankan fungsi utama mulai dari pengelolaan dokumen, pemrosesan knowledge base, retrieval informasi, generasi respons melalui Gemini API, hingga penyajian jawaban kepada pengguna. Pengujian fungsional terhadap sembilan skenario menunjukkan seluruh fungsi berhasil dijalankan dengan tingkat keberhasilan 100%. Pengujian respons juga menunjukkan bahwa sistem mampu menghasilkan jawaban yang relevan dan mengacu pada informasi yang tersedia pada knowledge base. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pendekatan RAG dapat diterapkan untuk mendukung layanan informasi akademik yang lebih interaktif dan berbasis bahasa alami pada tingkat fakultas.

title: RESEARCHING METHODS FOR THE AUTOMATIC DETECTION OF OFFENSIVE LANGUAGE BASED ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
abstract: This study explores artificial intelligence-based methods for the automatic detection of offensive language.The research focuses on the application of Natural Language Processing (NLP), machine learning, and deep learningtechniques to identify offensive, abusive, and inappropriate content in textual data. Particular attention is given to text preprocessing,feature extraction, text classification, and neural network-based approaches for improving the accuracy andefficiency of offensive language detection. The study highlights the potential of artificial intelligence to support safer digitalcommunication and enhance automated content moderation across online platforms

title: WP-031 — Persistent Memory as Architecture: Why Conversation Recall Transforms Autonomous Coherence
abstract: A system that cannot recall its own conversations cannot maintain coherence across sessions. We propose that **persistent conversation storage** is not a luxury enhancement but a foundational architectural requirement for lattice-coherent autonomous systems. Without it, geometric intelligence becomes amnesia-prone, unable to reference its own prior insight or validate consistency. This whitepaper documents the principle, its implementation necessity, and the evidence for why memory preservation directly strengthens lattice alignment.

title: CNN_SHAP_MASK: Explainable Mammography Classification and SHAP-Guided Segmentation (Интерпретируемая классификация маммографических изображений и сегментация с использованием SHAP)
abstract: CNN_SHAP_MASK v1.0.0 Первый публичный релиз исследовательского программного комплекса для интерпретируемого анализа маммографических изображений CDD-CESM с использованием сверточных нейронных сетей, методов объяснимого искусственного интеллекта и сегментации изображений. Основные возможности классификация изображений CDD-CESM на классы Normal / Benign / Malignant; обучение и оценка модели ResNet-18; построение визуальных объяснений с помощью Grad-CAM; вычисление карт важности SHAP; преобразование SHAP-карт в бинарные маски областей интереса; морфологическая обработка и построение convex hull; интеграция Segment Anything Model (SAM ViT-B); автоматическая сегментация с использованием SamAutomaticMaskGenerator; направляемая сегментация SAM с использованием SHAP-точек и bounding box; последовательный пайплайн CNN → SHAP → MASK → SAM; сохранение метрик, предсказаний, confusion matrix и визуализаций; поддержка запуска с готовыми весами без повторного обучения. Исследовательское назначение Проект исследует возможность использования методов объяснимого искусственного интеллекта не только для визуальной интерпретации решений CNN, но и в качестве источника пространственных подсказок для последующей сегментации медицинских изображений. SHAP-карты используются для локализации информативных областей и формирования масок и подсказок для Segment Anything Model. Ограничения Проект является исследовательским программным обеспечением и не предназначен для клинической диагностики или принятия медицинских решений. Датасет CDD-CESM и веса SAM не включаются непосредственно в релиз и должны использоваться в соответствии с условиями их исходных источников. Финансирование Исследование выполнено в рамках государственного задания Министерства науки и высшего образования Российской Федерации, тема № 124112200072-2. Funding: This research was carried out within the State Assignment of the Ministry of Science and Higher Education of the Russian Federation, topic No. 124112200072-2.

title: Looking Things Up Before Speaking: A Contemporary Synthesis Review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of RAG and retrieval as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

abstract: Today's finding is this: quantum teleportation is experimentally verified, and its scaling is governed strictly by entanglement fidelity, not by the classical bits used in the protocol. title: Title: Quantum-Inspired Algorithm for Non-Linear System Dynamics
abstract: Quantum-inspired algorithms represent a novel approach to modeling and predicting complex system dynamics, particularly those exhibiting non-linear behavior. This paper proposes a quantum-inspired algorithm designed to enhance the precision of predictions by mimicking quantum principles in approximating the system's evolution. We explore a framework that utilizes probabilistic elements and entanglement-like correlations to represent and navigate the system's trajectory. The core mechanism centers around a modified variational optimization technique, enhanced with quantum-like stochasticity, to achieve improved accuracy in complex simulations. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, introduces the core methodology, and provides preliminary results demonstrating its potential for advancing the field of system dynamics. The long-term goal is to establish a robust and efficient method for tackling challenging scenarios in diverse scientific and engineering domains.

title: Quantum Entanglement Machine Learning Algorithm
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum entanglement to enhance machine learning algorithms. The core claim posits the design of a novel machine learning algorithm predicated on leveraging quantum entanglement to significantly improve model performance. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this approach, outlining the key mechanisms and potential benefits. This work presents a framework for utilizing entanglement to potentially overcome limitations inherent in traditional machine learning models, focusing primarily on enhancing data representation and feature extraction. We acknowledge the significant challenges associated with implementing this concept and present preliminary results demonstrating the feasibility of this approach.

title: Brush-tailed Tree-rat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Brush-tailed Tree-rat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BTTIMA), designed to address a variety of optimization problems. The algorithm's core inspiration stems from the unique foraging and movement strategies observed in the brush-tailed tree-rat ( *Phaselis spp.*), a nocturnal marsupial known for its efficient navigation and resource exploitation within complex arboreal environments. BTTIMA incorporates elements of the tree-rat's exploratory behavior, memory retention, and adaptive movement patterns into its search process. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a dynamic representation of the search space resembling the tree-rat's spatial awareness. Key components include a memory mechanism that mimics the tree-rat's recollection of favorable foraging locations, a movement strategy based on the tree-rat's adaptive patrol patterns, and a self-adaptation mechanism that adjusts parameters based on the algorithm's performance. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. The results demonstrate that BTTIMA exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The algorithm's inherent adaptability and its grounding in a biologically inspired model suggest potential applicability across diverse optimization domains.

title: Title: Dynamical Constraint Optimization with Adaptive Random Forests
abstract: Dynamic Constraint Optimization (DCO) is a powerful technique for solving complex optimization problems, particularly those with highly irregular and evolving solution spaces. This paper introduces a novel approach combining adaptive random forests with dynamic constraint optimization, designed to effectively navigate these challenging landscapes. The core mechanism involves training a random forest on a limited dataset to guide the search, iteratively refining the solution space based on the forest's predictions, and applying constraints to ensure feasible and optimal solutions. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method through a series of challenging optimization problems, showcasing its ability to outperform traditional methods in terms of solution quality and computational efficiency. The research presents a framework for dynamically adapting to changing landscape features, making it well-suited for real-world applications requiring continuous optimization.

title: Quantum Information Geometric Field Theory
abstract: Quantum Information Geometric Field Theory (QIG-GFT) presents a novel approach to quantum information processing by leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement and superposition to simulate and manipulate geometric spaces. This theory aims to explore the unique geometric properties of quantum computation and quantum information storage through the integration of these quantum phenomena. The core mechanism centers on designing a quantum information processing framework that utilizes quantum entanglement and superposition to achieve geometric simulations, offering a fundamentally different perspective on information handling compared to traditional geometric field theories. This research investigates the potential of this framework to provide a more efficient and intuitive method for addressing complex quantum algorithms and data structures.

title: Fractal-Based Self-Organizing Algorithms for Parameter Tuning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel family of self-organizing algorithms designed to optimize complex systems by intelligently adapting to their inherent structure. The core of this approach lies in the implementation of a 'Fractal Parameter Weaver' – an algorithm that dynamically adjusts the parameters of a system based on its fractal characteristics. The study explores the potential of combining fractal geometry with self-organization to achieve a robust and adaptable optimization technique, specifically targeting parameter tuning within challenging environments. The goal is to design an algorithm that can effectively navigate and manipulate the parameter space, leading to improved performance and robustness.

title: Bayesian Non-Feedback Dynamics (BFND) for Statistical Physics
abstract: This paper introduces Bayesian Non-Feedback Dynamics (BFND) – a novel method for modeling complex, non-equilibrium systems by incorporating a latent state and a dynamic Bayesian inference framework. We demonstrate the efficacy of BFND in simulating systems exhibiting complex, non-linear behavior, addressing limitations of traditional approaches like direct numerical simulations. The core mechanism focuses on preventing catastrophic interference, ensuring the model's predictions remain accurate and stable. We present a comprehensive theoretical analysis and initial empirical validation, showcasing the potential of BFND to achieve significantly improved simulation accuracy and robustness. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the implications for various areas of statistical physics.

title: Low-power reservoir computing using parametrically excited spin waves
abstract: Spin waves provide a route to energy-efficient reservoir computing (RC), but realizing spin-wave reservoirs in the microwatt power range remains challenging. Here, we numerically demonstrate low-power RC based on parametric excitation in a single-crystal Fe thin film. Binary sequences are encoded as frequency-multiplexed microwave pulses through a strip antenna, and reservoir states are extracted from the magnetization power spectrum. At an input power of 2.2 mW, single-point detection provides parity-check and short-term-memory capacities of 1.71 and 1.72, respectively. Near the parametric threshold of 66 μW, the spin-wave response exhibits pronounced spatial diversity, reflecting the selective excitation of low-threshold modes. Although a single detection point captures only a limited portion of this state, multi-point detection exploits the spatial diversity to yield capacities of 1.56 and 1.63. These results show that spatial multiplexing maintains reservoir performance in low-power spin-wave systems and suggest a route toward microwatt-class spin-wave RC.

title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for the Board Game Splendor
abstract: Viele reale Entscheidungsprobleme sind durch verborgene Variablen, unvollständiges Wissen über andere Akteure und nicht-nullsummige Anreizstrukturen gekennzeichnet. Das Brettspiel Splendor verbindet diese Eigenschaften in einer Mehrspielerumgebung. Obwohl der Großteil des Spielzustands öffentlich sichtbar ist, bleiben die Reihenfolge der verdeckten Entwicklungskarten und verdeckt reservierte Karten anderer Spieler unbekannt. Gleichzeitig erfordert das Spiel langfristige Ressourcenplanung. Diese Arbeit untersucht, ob ein von AlphaZero inspiriertes Reinforcement-Learning-Verfahren auf diese teilweise beobachtbare Mehrspielerumgebung übertragen werden kann und ob neuronengestützte Planung sinnvoll mit einer Behandlung verborgener Information kombiniert werden kann. Zu diesem Zweck wurde eine Forschungsumgebung für Splendor entwickelt. Sie umfasst eine regelbasierte Spiel-Engine, eine Reinforcement-Learning-Schnittstelle, deterministische Initialisierung, Self-Play-Training und eine Turnierumgebung zur Evaluation. Der Agent kombiniert einen Transformer-basierten Zustandsencoder mit Monte-Carlo Tree Search (MCTS), wobei neuronale Policy- und Value-Vorhersagen die Suche steuern. Vektorwertige Value-Funktionen und MaxN-artige Backup-Regeln unterstützen Mehrpersonenspiele. Root Determinization approximiert die partielle Beobachtbarkeit durch die Simulation möglicher vollständiger Spielzustände. Das System wurde durch Self-Play trainiert und hinsichtlich Trainingsverlauf, Spielstärke, verborgener Information und unterschiedlicher Spielerzahlen evaluiert. Der Agent entwickelt im Verlauf des Trainings zunehmend kohärente und strukturierte Strategien und schneidet besser als zufällige beziehungsweise schwächere Baselines ab. Determinisierungsbasierte Planung verbessert zudem die Stabilität der Entscheidungen. Aufgrund begrenzter Rechenressourcen und Trainingsdauer wurde kein Expertenniveau erreicht. Die Ergebnisse zeigen jedoch, dass neuronengestützte Planung trotz Mehrspielerstruktur und partieller Beobachtbarkeit auf Splendor angewendet werden kann. Die Arbeit stellt eine reproduzierbare Forschungsumgebung und einen experimentellen Rahmen für Reinforcement Learning in teilweise beobachtbaren Multi-Agenten-Umgebungen bereit.

title: Izkušnje z uporabo lokalnih modelov LLM v sistemu COBISS
abstract: V preteklih letih smo v sistemu COBISS na podlagi velikih jezikovnih modelov in pristopa RAG razvili pametnega asistenta. Začetna implementacija je temeljila na uporabi zunanjih storitev (OpenAI), nato pa smo z uvedbo lokalnih modelov in knjižnice LangChain4j poenostavili razvoj in izboljšali razširljivost rešitev. Pozitivne izkušnje so potrdile našo strateško usmeritev k uporabi lokalno nameščenih odprtokodnih modelov, kar omogoča večji nadzor nad podatki, večjo zasebnost in nižje stroške. Umetno inteligenco smo razširili tudi na druga področja sistema COBISS. V aplikaciji COBISS Lib smo nadgradili obstoječe asistente in dodatno razvili več novih rešitev. Rešitve temeljijo na javanskem ekosistemu (Quarkus, LangChain4j) in arhitekturi mikrostoritev. V prispevku so predstavljene praktične izkušnje pri uvajanju lokalnih modelov in integraciji umetne inteligence v sistem COBISS.

title: OmniExtract: an automatic data extraction tool based on large language model and prompt engineering
abstract: Extracting structured information from documents or scientific papers is crucial for data sharing and retrieval. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in language understanding, and a number of LLM-based tools have been developed for extraction-oriented tasks. However, it's still difficult to find a universal and user-friendly tool for various practical extraction tasks. To address this challenge, we propose OmniExtract, an automatic data extraction tool with user-friendly configuration files that can adapt to various data extraction tasks. OmniExtract employs a prompt optimization method to refine task-specific prompts and achieve high extraction performance. It also supports comprehensive data extraction from both documents and tables, making it applicable to a broad range of data sources. Evaluation results show that OmniExtract obtains a high accuracy ~90% for three datasets. Furthermore, two additional data extraction applications of OmniExtract in real-world scenarios have been presented, achieving an accuracy of 92.21% and ~90% precision and recall, respectively. Specifically, OmniExtract can handle tabular files of various sizes and formats, and achieve over 99% precision and recall on table information extraction tasks. The data reliability performance shows that OmniExtract is a valuable tool for database updating. An online testing service is available at https://ngdc.cncb.ac.cn/omniextract/. The service can be deployed locally with the code in https://github.com/wyb39/OmniExtract.

title: Bridging Continual Learning and Green Cloud Computing: Foundations for Sustainable Time Series Anomaly Detection
abstract: Abstract While anomaly detection is essential for cloud computing and predictive maintenance, approaches that bridge continual learning with environmental sustainability remain largely unexplored. In production environments, evolving data distributions cause performance degradation of machine learning models, and naive adaptation may lead to forgetting of past patterns that are likely to reoccur. In this study, we formulate temporal concept-incremental anomaly detection for both univariate and multivariate time series. We introduce time-based and entity-based concept extraction strategies together with Wasserstein-distance diagnostics for inter- and intra-concept distribution drift, and define an evaluation protocol that measures detection quality, knowledge retention, and energy consumption. We further propose Selective Temporal Replay (STR), a replay strategy for autoencoder-based continual anomaly detection that combines diversity-based initialization, novelty-gated admission, retention-aware replacement, and age-weighted preservation of stored sequences. The empirical study comprises more than 5,400 experiments across four datasets, nine autoencoder architectures, and ten continual learning strategies. On Yahoo! A1, STR obtains the highest ROC-AUC in seven of the nine architectures and is the only strategy with positive backward transfer on all four datasets; under the smallest memory budgets, it obtains the highest ROC-AUC among replay methods on Yahoo! A1 and SMD. The sustainability analysis identifies when selective replay justifies its additional energy cost and when regularization-based continual learning strategies are preferable.

title: Dirac‐Like Quantum Dynamics and Tunable Non‐Markovian Effects in Bernal‐Stacked Bilayer Silicene
abstract: ABSTRACT We investigate quantum entanglement, coherence, non‐Markovianity, and teleportation in Bernal‐stacked bilayer silicene (BBS) described by a tight‐binding Hamiltonian including mass and voltage terms. The noiseless dynamics is mapped onto a Dirac equation with pseudovector and tensor fields, while environmental noise is modeled as random fluctuations in the bias voltage and mass. Using open quantum system techniques, we demonstrate that the bias ratio, defined as the ratio between the bias voltage parameter and the interlayer coupling strength, serves as a powerful control parameter governing the quantum properties of the system. Entanglement entropy and quantum coherence exhibit a clear transition from pronounced oscillatory behavior at weak coupling to stable, maximally entangled and coherent states at strong coupling. The non‐Markovianity measure peaks at intermediate coupling, where memory effects and information backflow are maximally enhanced, marking a transition from non‐Markovian to Markovian dynamics as environmental memory diminishes. Under non‐Markovian noise, increasing the noise bandwidth parameter enhances the resilience of quantum correlations. When the noise bandwidth exceeds a certain threshold, the teleportation fidelity exhibits a significant enhancement, reflecting the improved robustness of the quantum state‐transfer dynamics. Our results demonstrate that BBS provides a versatile theoretical platform for investigating how the bias voltage and the noise bandwidth parameter influence entanglement, coherence, non‐Markovian dynamics, and teleportation fidelity.
